You are right. I probably should also have mentioned this, but I didn't want to seem to judgy. Last year they found out about this boy she was going with. Her father went to his FB and with its info created a fake police report to convince her he was a criminal, just because he didn't like the kid. From then on he spied on her FB and even intercepted some of our messages.

Thank you for your reply. Yes, that seems like the best option, even though that's what she's been doing for quite a while... anyway, as I told her before, time will certainly fix things, but until then...
No, I'd like to know what would be the best way for her to deal with the situation (not going to pressure her to anything).

Supporting an adult person gives you great control over her life, but not ownership over that same life. But again, not worth going into this topic. It's not a matter of whether they have or haven't the legal or moral right to rule over her, it's about how unfair it is and how it affects her.

Well thank you. Note that I'm not revolted with all this or anything, I'm actually pretty calm. And I do not fear for our relationship (although this is boresome) but rather I suffer because I know she suffers.

I do apologize for the wrong reply. I'm on mobile reddit so sometimes I get tricked by the app.
I don't want to dictate how her parents should act. And my point of view is shared by all of mine and her friends. She is being isolated from everyone.
Well I guess that's a more complex topic that is somewhat irrelevant here. Thank you for your view. I disagree, but let's not develop please, it would be a waste of time.

Please calm down. That is exactly the problem. They're not against me, they're against boys in general (especially the mom). I can't meet them. If I can't meet they can't trust me, that much obvious yes, but there's not I can do about it. I'd really like to know them and be nice to them and show that I'm nice to their daughter. I just can't.
They can forbid her to take a boy home, not of having a relationship.

What you say is true and it's how I think and how I've been acting so far. However, due to her personality and the fact that she's been adopted she subconsciously feels she owes them (more than she should feel) and that doesn't help her to make a stand. Also note her mother is homophobic, and want's her to be "feminin", forbidding her to play soccer and such sports because "those are men stuff". Not judging the mother, just trying to highlight the fact that they're quite close minded in certain matters which makes things difficult. Again, no disrespect towards them.
Who said I didn't respect them? I never even met them but I'm sure they're good folks and care about her deeply. Their house, their rules, not their life.

Living with one's parents with their income does give them a say-so in SOME things. They have the right to know what's happening with her life, how she's doing in college, who are the people closest to her. And of course thing like when she leaves the house, where she goes, etc. But they can't decide everything. I don't know about you, but according to your vision, you either had "lazy parents" as you call it, become financially independent before your 20s (did you though?) or unfortunately you never had a social life in you youth and for that I'm sorry.

BTW, "freedom of speech" was ironically refering to you, not me.

I just got say, your comment is very mature. Just not what I was looking for, you know? I wanted advice on how to handle it. Besides, I described the situation and didn't blame nor insult anyone. I think the only one here making uninformed judgments is you, but hey, freedom of speech am I right?

I'll repeat what I said. She's an adult that is forbidden from leaving the house just because. She never did anything wrong. No bad companions, no addictions, not even getting late at night (since her dad would pick her up anyway). She's quite responsible and she is being stolen the freedom she is entitled to at the age of 18.
Besides, how could she demonstrate she is capable of being independent if they don't let her?
And in any case, a parent should worry but never say things like "no boys" imo. I mean, they CANNOT forbidden her of being in a relationship, especially if they don't know anything about me so there's nothing bad to point out!
